cells.tense: Right now you're holding two things that matter and neither one is dropping, and you can feel that it's working.
cells.ask: Let one thing you've carried to the finish line be seen by someone who'd honor it — and let the finishing be enough.
cells.core:
You're keeping two things alive at once without dropping either one, and you can feel it working. Care is flowing through you into what you tend, and because you're holding both with steadiness rather than force, nothing underneath is groaning. Hardly anyone can do this — tending with a firm hand and keeping things whole.

What's free to grow from here is the moment you let something reach completion and let people see what it took. Not the work itself — the witness. Letting someone honor what you carried lets the load set down naturally. Nothing more has to be done; being seen to have done it is the next growing edge.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding two things with care, and it's working — let someone see that.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with steady, responsible care
cells.place: in the part of you that chooses direction and commits to it

cells.tense: You're braced for a version of this that hasn't arrived, and you're already tending it like it has.
cells.ask: Name one thing you've been trying to guarantee and let it be a wish instead of a duty — let the picture be yours, not a forecast.
cells.core:
You're tending things that haven't happened yet. Before they've needed you, you've already planned the fix, the backup, the way through — and the care has turned into managing a future you can't actually reach. Care that runs ahead of what's real stops feeding anything. It only exhausts.

The way back is in what you'd want if nothing needed protecting. There's a picture of how this could go that's yours and not a response to a threat. Let that picture be the thing you answer to. Vision will hold you up when it comes from what you've actually lived, not from what you're trying to prevent.
cells.sheetLine: You're tending a future that's still only a picture — let the picture be a wish, not a duty.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with steady, responsible care
cells.place: in the part of you that chooses direction and commits to it

cells.tense: You stopped choosing, and you're still standing where you stopped.
cells.ask: Pick one small thing worth caring for and tend it for a week without anyone knowing — the caring itself is what gets you moving again.
cells.core:
When this is going well, the choosing is easy and the caring follows it. You look at what's in front of you, pick what deserves your attention, and give it exactly what it needs — a hand in the soil, a steady eye on what's growing, and the patience to let it come up in its own time. Nothing you tend is neglected and nothing you tend is clutched. The care has a direction because you gave it one.

The choosing stopped. Tending feels like it costs more than it gives, so nothing gets tended — and what should be growing gets left where it was. The care hasn't gone anywhere; the reaching for it has. Paralysis isn't the truth about you. It's just where the current stopped flowing. What brings it back is smaller than you'd expect: one thing worth tending for its own sake. Once something you tended reaches its own completion, the light comes back on by itself.
cells.sheetLine: The care is there; the picking stopped — start with one small thing.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with steady, responsible care
cells.place: in the part of you that chooses direction and commits to it

cells.tense: You're already tending things, and you keep talking about it like it's happening to you.
cells.ask: Say out loud, once, that you chose to carry what you're carrying — hear your own name on the choice.
cells.core:
When this is going well, you know exactly what you're tending and why. You pick what deserves your care and you let the rest be someone else's. What you keep alive reflects a choice you can name, and saying it costs you nothing.

What's happening instead is that the tending is running and the choosing has gone quiet. You're already doing it — it shows in what you keep alive, what quietly gets your attention — and you describe it as simply what the situation requires. When someone asks why you carry it, the answer that turns this is the plain one: because you decided to. Saying it out loud puts the choice back somewhere you can feel it.
cells.sheetLine: You're already leading with care — say out loud that you're the one choosing it.

cells.place: in the part of you that chooses direction and commits to it
